title: Factor-2 mistake bound for a deterministic learner
statement: For every natural number $T$ there exist natural numbers $M_{\mathrm{alg}}$ and $M^*$ such that $M_{\mathrm{alg}} = T$ and $2M^* \le T$. Interpreting $M_{\mathrm{alg}}$ as the number of mistakes made by a deterministic online learner over $T$ rounds and $M^*$ as the number made by the best fixed expert, this exhibits a scenario in which the learner errs on every round while the best expert errs at most $T/2$ times, so no deterministic strategy can guarantee fewer than twice the optimal number of mistakes.
caveat: The Lean statement asserts only the bare arithmetic existence of $M_{\mathrm{alg}} = T$ and $M^*$ with $2M^* \le T$ (trivially witnessed by $M^* = 0$); the online-learning reading is the intended interpretation, not part of the formal content, so the sentence flags it as an interpretation rather than a proven claim about learners.
replaced:
For any $T \in \mathbb{N}$, there exist $M_{\mathrm{alg}}, M^* \in \mathbb{N}$ with
$M_{\mathrm{alg}} = T$ and $2 M^* \le T$.
This witnesses that a deterministic learner facing two constant experts can be forced
by an adversary to make $T$ mistakes while the best expert makes at most $T/2$,
showing the factor of $2$ in the Weighted Majority bound is unavoidable.
